> 武侯勞之曰：「先生病矣！苦於山林之勞，故乃肯見於寡人。」

The Marquis of Wei greets him: sir, you are worn out — the hardship of the hills and woods — and so you have consented to see me.

徐無鬼 answers: I am the one who will 勞 you. What makes you think you are the tired one?

## One character, two directions

勞: to labor, and to comfort someone for their labor — 慰勞.

The Marquis uses it the first way: you have suffered. 徐無鬼 turns it: the suffering is yours, and it has not started yet. The whole chapter's opening hinge is this single word rotating.

## 盈 and 黜: both are illness

君將盈耆欲，長好惡，則性命之情病矣 — indulge the appetites, grow the likes and dislikes, and the actual state of your life falls ill.

君將黜耆欲，掔好惡，則耳目病矣 — remove the appetites, drag away the likes and dislikes, and the senses fall ill.

Add, and the life is sick. Subtract, and the senses are sick. The first verdict of the chapter is that both operations are diseases — because both treat the person as something to be adjusted.

## 超然不對

超然: abstracted, at a loss. 不對: no reply.

The Marquis's first response is silence, and this chapter, like 田子方, records being hit as silence rather than agreement.

## The dogs, and 國馬

Three grades. The lowest: 執飽而止，是狸德也 — stops when full, which is a cat's virtue. The middle: 若視日 — gaze fixed like looking at the sun. The next: 若亡其一 — as though it has lost itself.

Then the one that meets every measure: 直者中繩，曲者中鉤，方者中矩，圓者中規. All four standards satisfied — and this is the 國馬, the state horse. Good, and not the best.

The best is described differently: 成材，若恤若失 — of native build, and yet absent, as though slackened. 超軼絕塵，不知其所 — it passes beyond, kicks up no dust, and no one knows where it has gone.

Four standards met is the definition of 合. And the chapter quietly files that as second grade.

## 跫然: a footstep

聞人足音跫然而喜矣 — to hear the sound of a person's step and be glad.

This is in the passage on the exile: weeds blocking the animal trails, a man alone in the emptiness, and then footsteps. 跫然 is the lightest word in the chapter and the heaviest: the joy is not at company, it is at any evidence that one is not the only thing here.

## The test

Take one thing you are currently repairing in yourself — a habit to add or a habit to cut. Then apply the chapter's first verdict: is this 盈 or 黜? Both, it says, are illness — because both begin from the premise that the person needs adjusting. Then apply the dog test: does your standard have four measures that can all be satisfied? If so, it describes 國馬, and the best thing in the chapter would not pass it.
